 The Honourable Smt. Justice Lalitha Kanneganti

Judgment:

Aggrieved by the award dated 19.09.2008 in O.P.No.544 of 2005 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-III Additional District Judge (FAC), Khammam, the insurance company has preferred this appeal.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-III Additional District Judge (FAC), Khammam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Having heard Mr. P. Harinath Gupta, learned counsel for the Appellant/insurance company and Mr. Nageshwar Rao Repakula, learned counsel for the respondent/claimant, perused the entire material on record.

3. The claim petition was filed under Section 166 of M.V Act seeking compensation of Rs.1,00,000/-
for the injuries sustained by the claimant in the motor accident that took place on 05.03.2005.
The Court below has awarded an amount of Rs.78,262/- and directed the insurance company and owner of the vehicle to pay the same jointly and severally.
The case of the insurance company is that the claimant was travelling in a goods vehicle and he was a gratuitous passenger and as per the settled law, he is not entitled for compensation.
4. Learned counsel for the insurance company submitted that as per Ex.B-1/Policy, it is only the driver, who is covered.

Learned counsel for the claimant submitted that as per Section 147 of the Act, the owner of the goods or his representative is covered under the policy and as the claimant being the owner of the goods, he is entitled for compensation.
6.

The court below while discussing the issue of granting compensation has observed that PW.1 is owner of the goods in the vehicle and as no sufficient evidence is adduced before the court below to prove the same, the court below has held that the insurer and owner of the vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
7. There is no dispute about the fact that the claimant is the owner of the goods and hence, the court below has rightly held that the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.
